methodological_rigor.justification: Cross-sectional review of 136 Canadian Cancer Trials Group protocols activated 1999-2025. Descriptive analysis of HIV eligibility language (included, not mentioned, excluded) with chi-square tests. Multivariable analysis identifies associations with immune checkpoint blockade (p=0.039) and industry support (p=0.014). However, limited statistical modeling, no adjustment for multiple confounders, no confidence intervals for prevalence estimates. Descriptive epidemiology only.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Addresses equity in cancer clinical trial design regarding HIV inclusion. Identifies barriers to enrollment of people living with HIV. However, study documents policy/protocol patterns rather than clinical outcomes. Limited direct clinical relevance; primarily policy-focused. LoE very low given descriptive methodology.

reporting_quality.justification: Describes trial selection, abstraction process, and analytical approach. Results presented as proportions with chi-square tests. However, no confidence intervals provided for prevalence estimates. No explicit STROBE adherence. Protocol data from CCTG available but study data availability not mentioned.

novelty_literature.justification: Study documents HIV exclusion patterns in clinical trials; topic of equity and inclusion well-established in literature. Previous recommendations from NIH/Friends of Cancer Research (2017) addressed unjustified HIV exclusions. Study primarily audits compliance with existing guidance rather than proposing novel approaches. Limited new knowledge.

writing_presentation.justification: Readable manuscript presenting policy audit findings. Clear description of trial characteristics (solid vs hematologic, therapy type, phase). Results straightforward: 36% included, 40% not mentioned, 24% excluded PLWH. Discussion appropriately emphasizes equity concerns and aligns with emerging guidance. However, limited analytical depth.

key_strengths: Addresses important equity issue: HIV inclusion in cancer clinical trials
First Canadian national assessment documenting adherence to NIH/Friends of Cancer Research inclusion guidance
Identifies trial characteristics associated with HIV exclusion (immune checkpoint therapy, industry support)
Clear policy implications for future trial design
key_concerns: Purely descriptive cross-sectional audit without analytical rigor; limited statistical modeling
No confidence intervals for prevalence estimates; chi-square tests without adjustment for multiple comparisons
Small sample (N=136 trials) may limit representativeness of broader oncology trial landscape
Limited novelty; HIV exclusion patterns and need for inclusion previously documented in literature
No proposed interventions or solutions beyond identifying pattern of exclusion
Missing important details: reasons for exclusion not abstracted, actual eligibility criteria not analyzed
chief_reviewer.rationale: Low-evidence policy audit documenting HIV exclusion patterns in Canadian cancer trials. Appropriate for Tier 4 or policy/commentary venues. Limited statistical rigor and novelty; documents problem without novel solutions or mechanistic insight. Contributes to equity discourse but lacks methodological sophistication.
